title: Шеф идёт на поклон к Елене  (The Chef Swallows His Pride with Elena)

segments.t: After ordering his cooks to start prepping immediately, Viktor Petrovich hurries over to Arcobaleno to find Elena Pavlovna. Swallowing his pride, he apologizes for his foolish remarks about male principles and admits that he urgently needs her help to save the wedding banquet.
Живо за работу.
Лен, Лена.
Про работу.
Это ж не про нас.
Это я так, для примера.
Что был неправ.
Но сейчас мне нужна твоя помощь.
Как же твои мужские принципы?
Ты же никогда не хотел зависеть от женщин.
Лен, я не хочу сейчас выяснять отношения.
А я тоже не собиралась выяснять отношения.
Мне в голову не могло прийти.
Кто знал.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
Живо за работу.
'Get to work, lively now!' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'right now' and 'behind' in a few short words. Elena answers right away.
Лен, Лена.
'Lena, wait, Lena.' The meaning hinges on 'Lena' working together with 'Lena' in spoken Russian.
Про работу.
'I was talking about work.' Notice how Russian expresses 'about' and 'work' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Это ж не про нас.
'That was not about the two of us.' Elena anchors the line on 'this', while 'us' completes the thought. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Это я так, для примера.
'I only said that as an example.' In Russian, the idea of 'this' flows naturally into 'example' without extra filler words.
Что был неправ.
'To admit that I was wrong.' Elena anchors the line on 'what', while 'wrong' completes the thought.
Но сейчас мне нужна твоя помощь.
'And right now I really need your help.' Chef Viktor addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'help'. Elena answers right away.
Как же твои мужские принципы?
'What happened to your famous male principles?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'how' and finishing on 'principles'.
Ты же никогда не хотел зависеть от женщин.
'You never wanted to depend on women, remember?' In Russian, the idea of 'you' flows naturally into 'women' without extra filler words.
Лен, я не хочу сейчас выяснять отношения.

'Lena, I do not want to argue about our relationship right now.' Notice how Russian expresses 'Lena' and 'relationships' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
А я тоже не собиралась выяснять отношения.
'I was not planning to argue about our relationship either.' The meaning hinges on 'and' working together with 'relationships' in spoken Russian.
Мне в голову не могло прийти.
'It never would have crossed my mind.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'for me' before landing on 'to come'.
Кто знал.
'Who could have known?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'who' and finishing on 'knew'. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
